html:
The Chollima movement was a campaign launched by Kim Il Sung in 1958 to drive North Korean workers to build the economy at the speed of Chollima, a winged horse of legend said to cover a thousand li in a day.

After the Korean War left the North in ruins, Soviet and Chinese aid and mass labour rebuilt its factories, mines and cities very fast. Work teams competed to beat targets and won titles as Chollima brigades. Farms were collectivised by 1958.

For a time it worked: into the 1960s North Korea's economy grew faster than the South's. But the campaigns wore people out and favoured heavy industry, and growth slowed in the 1970s. The movement became the model for later speed battles, and the Chollima statue still towers over Pyongyang. It went hand in hand with the ideology of Juche, self-reliance, and ended in the famine of the 1990s.
sum: The Chollima movement was a campaign launched by Kim Il Sung in 1958 to drive North Korean workers to build the economy at the speed of Chollima, a winged horse of legend said to cover a thousand li in a day.
